entities.summary: Columba of Spain was a 9th-century entrepreneur and religious figure who played a significant role in the development of Córdoba, Spain, during the Classical era. Born in the 8th century, Columba is known for his leadership in the establishment of the first Moorish school in Córdoba, which became a hub for Islamic learning and culture. His legacy extended to the establishment of the first Christian church in Córdoba, which was later converted into a mosque by the Moors. The city of Córdoba would go on to become a major center of learning and culture during the Islamic Golden Age, influencing the development of Western civilization. Despite the passage of time, Columba's contributions to the city's growth and cultural development continue to be celebrated today. The Moorish school he founded remains a testament to his vision and leadership, with many historians considering him a key figure in the spread of Islamic knowledge and culture during the Middle Ages.
